sentences: Have you heard the news?
هل سمعت الخبر؟
My sister has just had a baby girl.
رُزقت أختي للتو بطفلة.
I've already finished my report.
أنهيت تقريري بالفعل.
Has Omar arrived yet? — No, not yet.
هل وصل عمر حتى الآن؟ — لا، ليس بعد.
I haven't read the article yet.
لم أقرأ المقال بعد.
Nour has got a promotion! — Congratulations!
حصلت نور على ترقية! — مبروك!
Prices have risen a lot recently.
ارتفعت الأسعار كثيرًا مؤخرًا.
There was a fire in the city centre last night.
شبّ حريق في وسط المدينة ليلة أمس.
According to the report, nobody was hurt.
وفقًا للتقرير، لم يُصَب أحد.
I failed my driving test. — Oh, I'm sorry to hear that.
رسبت في اختبار القيادة. — يؤسفني سماع ذلك.

grammar.intro_en:
Present perfect = a past action connected to now, with no finished time (I've lost my keys. = I don't have them now.)
just = a very short time ago · already = before now, sooner than expected · yet = until now (in negatives and questions, at the end)
Past simple = a finished time: yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago, When …?
grammar.intro_ar: المتعلم العربي يقول «لسه واصل» بالماضي البسيط: I just arrived (وهذا شائع في الإنجليزية الأمريكية)، لكن في الإنجليزية البريطانية نقول I've just arrived. والخطأ الأكبر: استخدام present perfect مع كلمة تدل على وقت منتهٍ مثل yesterday أو ago أو last: I have seen him yesterday ✗ → I saw him yesterday ✔. وانتبه لمكان الكلمات: just و already قبل التصريف الثالث، و yet في آخر الجملة.

rows: Have you seen the news today?
Did you see the news last night?
Prices went up two months ago.

notes: Questions with When …? and What time …? take the past simple: When did you hear the news? (NOT When have you heard …?)
News often starts with the present perfect, then gives the details in the past simple: There has been an accident on the Ring Road. It happened at 8 a.m.

write_speak: Write & Speak — “My news”: write an email of 80–100 words to a friend you haven't seen for a long time. Give three pieces of news (use just, already and yet) and add details in the past simple. Then read it aloud as if you are telling your friend on the phone.
other:
Example: Dear Mona,
How are you? I'm sorry I haven't written for so long. I've been very busy, and I have lots of news! First, we've just moved house. We left our old flat in Shubra two weeks ago and now we live in Sheikh Zayed. Also, my brother has got engaged! The party was last Friday and it was wonderful. I've also started a new job, but I haven't met all my colleagues yet. Have you finished your exams yet? Write soon and tell me your news.
Love,
Nour
